summary: A BBN note observing that the FTP and Remote Job Entry protocols had grown very similar, each with a control connection for commands and a data connection for uninterpreted data. It suggests merging them into a single data transfer protocol and lists advantages beyond simplicity. It is a proposal, not a specification.

eli5.summary: Two programs for moving things between computers worked almost the same way, so someone suggested combining them into one.

subtitle: A proposal to merge FTP and RJE into a unified data transfer protocol.

tldr.problem: By 1973, both FTP and Remote Job Entry had evolved to be very similar: a control connection for commands and a data connection for uninterpreted data. Sites had to implement both protocols separately.
tldr.mechanism: Merge FTP and RJE into a single data transfer protocol with optional command subsets: general system commands, parameter settings, data control, file operations, and job execution. Implementations could support just file transfer or add job execution as needed.
tldr.outcome: The proposal was not immediately adopted, but influenced protocol design thinking. Modern systems handle file transfer and job submission as separate concerns using different protocols.

today: This RFC was a proposal, not a specification, and was not adopted. Modern practice treats file transfer and batch job submission as separate protocols, handled by different systems (SFTP for files, schedulers for jobs).

sections.title: The Similar Protocols
sections.content: By March 1973, FTP and Remote Job Entry (RJE) had developed in parallel, each solving different problems but using the same underlying architecture. Both used a control connection for commands and a data connection for uninterpreted data. Both dealt with authentication, parameter setup, and data transfer. New concepts like the "hot card reader" were added to one or the other, but were generally applicable to both.
sections.eli5: Two different programs for sending files and jobs between computers were doing almost the same basic things.

sections.title: Unified Data Transfer Protocol
sections.content:
The proposal suggests creating a single data transfer protocol with modular command sets. The basic set includes general system commands (like USER, HELP), parameter settings (TYPE, STRU), data control (ABORT, REIN), file operations (STOR, RETR, LIST), and job execution (INPUT, OUTPUT, CHANGE). A site could implement the file transfer subset, or add job execution commands for full RJE support.

This approach would reduce code duplication: sites need only build one server program, falling back to "command not implemented" for unsupported subsets. It eliminates the need for separate FTP and RJE user and server processes and Telnet connections.
sections.eli5: Build one program with optional pieces: basic file transfer works for everyone, but some computers can also handle job requests.

sections.title: Advantages Beyond Simplicity
sections.content:
The proposal identifies several benefits beyond code simplicity. First, new ideas and concepts would be shared by all users and servers. A RJE user could transfer a deck of cards to storage on another machine using the "hot card reader" concept, previously only in RJE. Second, deployment flexibility: users at traditional RJE stations could store files on machines supporting only basic file transfer, then later connect to a batch server and instruct it to pull the files.

This design separated the concerns of file storage and batch job execution, allowing more flexible deployment architectures.
sections.eli5: New features would work everywhere, and computers could store files without running jobs, and run jobs later from stored files.
